text:
olivia-sre: customer (acme-inc) exported audit events and flagged a KMS decrypt they didn't expect at 03:14 UTC. they attached a tiny snippet, asking us to confirm origin.

maya-sec: can you drop the snippet here and the customer workspace id? :eyes: we need to validate actor/principal mapping.

olivia-sre: workspace=acme-prod. snippet pasted below:
```
2026-03-20T03:14:12Z  event=KMS_DECRYPT  principal=service:svc-retriever@acme-inc  key_id=key-prod-7f9a  request_id=req-0a1b2c
2026-03-20T03:14:12Z  event=AUDIT  actor=svc-provisioner@redwood  action=role.assign  target=svc-retriever@acme-inc  role=workspace.kms_reader
```

maya-sec: thanks. timeline question: was the role.assign event in our audit pipeline or the customer's? the snippet mixes two sources.

tim-audit: running a scoped query on our audit_events index for target=svc-retriever@acme-inc +- 10m. will also pull KMS gateway logs.

raj: FYI there was a scheduled automation yesterday from svc-provisioner (deploy pipeline) that granted short-lived roles for onboarding. I can pull the run id.

kms-bot: KMS_GATEWAY: decrypt request logged: request_id=req-0a1b2c principal=service:svc-retriever@acme-inc key=key-prod-7f9a result=OK latency_ms=27

tim-audit: query results: 3 events match.
- 2026-03-20T03:13:55Z audit: actor=svc-provisioner@redwood action=role.assign target=svc-retriever@acme-inc role=workspace.kms_reader metadata={duration=10m request_id=req-0a1b00}
- 2026-03-20T03:14:12Z kms: decrypt request req-0a1b2c principal=svc-retriever@acme-inc key=key-prod-7f9a
- 2026-03-20T03:14:13Z audit: user=svc-retriever@acme-inc action=read object=secrets/obj-42 request_id=req-0a1b2d

maya-sec: correlation looks tight: provisioner issued a short-lived role ~17s before decrypt. need to confirm the role TTL vs actual usage window. also verify the actor identity (was svc-provisioner itself properly authenticated).

olivia-sre: customer is worried about lateral access; they want a human-readable timeline to share with their compliance team. can we produce a validated timeline that maps our audit_event ids to their export rows? we should also redact internal request headers.

tim-audit: I'll assemble a minimal timeline artifact: map of {timestamp, event_id, source, actor_principal, action, key_id/request_id}. will include hashes for blob crosswalk. planning to push to private S3 share and send signed link.

raj: quick note — the automation run id is deploy-run-4832, started by svc-platform@redwood. I can attach the run logs showing the role.assign TTL=600s.

maya-sec: next steps: 1) tim produce timeline artifact and validation notes 2) raj attach run logs and proof the assign was through the authorized pipeline 3) confirm KMS audit shows no anomalous key policy changes 4) prepare one-paragraph customer summary + suggested remediation (shorter TTL or more granular roles).

olivia-sre: thanks team, customer asked for ETA ~2h. I'll tell them we're investigating and will share a timeline. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy pipeline run deploy-run-4832 completed (success) by svc-platform@redwood at 2026-03-20T03:13:45Z

tim-audit: timeline artifact uploaded to s3://redwood-forensics/acme-prod/1998765432/timeline.json (signed link provided to SE). I've redacted x-forwarded headers and included mapping to customer's exported rows.

maya-sec: will review artifact and sign off before we send customer-facing validation. tagging @olivia-sre to coordinate delivery.

olivia-sre: acknowledged. I'll draft the summary and attach the signed timeline once you confirm.

maya-sec: quick reminder for follow-up: recommend we add an eval alert for provisioning events that grant workspace.kms_reader role so we can detect unexpected grants across customer workspaces.

olivia-sre: noted — filing follow-up ticket in sec backlog.
